study.title: Heard From the First Day
study.subtitle: Why are some prayers answered quickly while others seem delayed? This study explores the spiritual warfare behind prayer, examining Daniel's 21-day wait and what it teaches us about persistence in prayer.
study.theme: God hears our prayers from the first day. Delays are real, the enemy is real, and yet the enemy is limited, the battle is spiritual, and every prayer is kept and answered in God's timing.
reflection_questions: What have I been praying about that feels delayed? Have I stopped praying?
Where might I be fighting flesh and blood when the battle is spiritual?
Which piece of the armour am I neglecting?
Like Job, can I worship in the middle of loss, before the restoration?
Like Paul, can I receive "My grace is sufficient" if the answer is different from my ask?
What does it change to know my words were heard from the first day?

content.text: Daniel prayed and fasted three weeks. Heaven answered on day one, and yet the answer took 21 days to arrive. Why?

In those days I Daniel was mourning three full weeks. I ate no pleasant bread, neither came flesh nor wine in my mouth, neither did I anoint myself at all, till three whole weeks were fulfilled. (Daniel 10:2-3)
But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me one and twenty days: but, lo, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me; and I remained there with the kings of Persia. (Daniel 10:13)
Then said he, Knowest thou wherefore I come unto thee? and now will I return to fight with the prince of Persia: and when I am gone forth, lo, the prince of Grecia shall come. (Daniel 10:20)
Notice:
The prayer was not stopped. It was
heard
the first day (v12)
The
answer
was resisted in the spiritual realm (v13)
Michael came to help. Heaven sends reinforcement
Daniel kept praying and fasting the whole 21 days without knowing any of this

sections.heading: Know the Enemy: Names of Satan

content.text: His names reveal how he operates: he accuses, tempts, lies, deceives, and blinds.
Name
KJV wording
Reference
Satan (adversary)
Satan standing at his right hand to resist him
Zechariah 3:1, Job 1:6
The Devil
that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan
Revelation 12:9
Lucifer
How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning!
Isaiah 14:12
Anointed cherub
Thou art the anointed cherub that covereth
Ezekiel 28:14 (King of Tyrus, 28:12-17)
The serpent
Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field
Genesis 3:1
The great dragon
And the great dragon was cast out
Revelation 12:9
Deceiver
which deceiveth the whole world
Revelation 12:9
Accuser
the accuser of our brethren is cast down
Revelation 12:10
Beelzebub
Beelzebub the prince of the devils
Matthew 12:24
Belial
what concord hath Christ with Belial?
2 Corinthians 6:15
Prince of this world
now shall the prince of this world be cast out
John 12:31
Prince of the power of the air
the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience
Ephesians 2:2
God of this world
the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not
2 Corinthians 4:4
Liar and murderer
He was a murderer from the beginning... he is a liar, and the father of it
John 8:44
The tempter
And when the tempter came to him
Matthew 4:3
That wicked one
that wicked one toucheth him not
1 John 5:18
The enemy
The enemy that sowed them is the devil
Matthew 13:39
Adversary, roaring lion
your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about
1 Peter 5:8
Angel of light (disguise)
Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light
2 Corinthians 11:14
Abaddon / Apollyon
the angel of the bottomless pit
Revelation 9:11 (debated whether Satan or a demon under him)
His kingdom has rulers.
The prince of Persia and prince of Grecia (Daniel 10:13, 20) are best read as spiritual rulers under Satan over territories, not names of Satan himself.
And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven. (Luke 10:18)
Satan attacks, and yet he must ask permission and stay inside the boundary God sets.
Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side? (Job 1:10)
And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand. (Job 1:12)
And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, he is in thine hand; but save his life. (Job 2:6)
How the attack came:
Sabeans took the oxen and asses and slew the servants (1:14-15)
Fire of God fell from heaven and burned the sheep and servants (1:16)
Chaldeans took the camels (1:17)
A great wind struck the house and killed his sons and daughters (1:18-19)
Sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown (2:7)
His wife: Curse God, and die (2:9)
The attacks came stacked, one messenger still speaking when the next arrived. The goal was for Job to curse God (1:11, 2:5).
Job's response:

Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD. In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly. (Job 1:21-22)
The restoration:
And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before. (Job 42:10)
The same pattern with Peter:

Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren. (Luke 22:31-32)
Already defeated:
And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it. (Colossians 2:15)
Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. (James 4:7)
Paul explains what Daniel experienced. The fight is spiritual, and the last piece of the armour is prayer.

Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might. Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places. (Ephesians 6:10-12)
Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand. (Ephesians 6:13)
The whole armour (6:14-17):
Loins girt about with truth
Breastplate of righteousness
Feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace
Shield of faith, to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked
Helmet of salvation
Sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God
Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints. (Ephesians 6:18)
Connect it:
"Principalities" and "rulers of the darkness" in Ephesians 6:12 are the same kind of power as the prince of Persia in Daniel 10:13. Daniel's 21 days of prayer and fasting is Ephesians 6:18 in action.
Scripture is full of people who waited. Each delay had a reason, and none of them were forgotten.
Delay that requires persistence
Elijah prays for rain (1 Kings 18:43-44, James 5:17-18)

And said to his servant, Go up now, look toward the sea. And he went up, and looked, and said, There is nothing. And he said, Go again seven times. And it came to pass at the seventh time, that he said, Behold, there ariseth a little cloud out of the sea, like a man's hand. (1 Kings 18:43-44)
The persistent widow (Luke 18:1-8)
And he spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint. (Luke 18:1)
And shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him, though he bear long with them? I tell you that he will avenge them speedily. (Luke 18:7-8)
The friend at midnight (Luke 11:5-10)
And I say unto you, Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you. (Luke 11:9)
The Canaanite woman (Matthew 15:21-28)
But he answered her not a word. (Matthew 15:23)
O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt. And her daughter was made whole from that very hour. (Matthew 15:28)
Delay for a bigger purpose
Lazarus (John 11:1-44)
This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God might be glorified thereby. (John 11:4)
When he had heard therefore that he was sick, he abode two days still in the same place where he was. (John 11:6)
Said I not unto thee, that, if thou wouldest believe, thou shouldest see the glory of God? (John 11:40)
Martha said "if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died" (11:21). Jesus wasn't late. He was waiting for something bigger than healing: resurrection.
Jairus's daughter, twelve years old (Mark 5:21-43, Luke 8:40-56)
Jairus begs Jesus to come. On the way, Jesus stops for the woman with an issue of blood twelve years (Mark 5:25). During that stop, word comes that the girl has died.
Be not afraid, only believe. (Mark 5:36)
And straightway the damsel arose, and walked; for she was of the age of twelve years. (Mark 5:42)
One woman waited twelve years, one girl had lived twelve years. Someone else's breakthrough delayed his, and yet both were made whole.
The man born blind (John 9:1-7)
Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him. (John 9:3)

The disciples asked if it was his sin or his parents'. Jesus said neither. Scripture doesn't record anyone praying for his sight, so use this one for the *purpose* behind a long affliction, not for delayed prayer.
Long waits on a promise
Abraham (Genesis 12:4, 21:5)
Abram was seventy and five years old when he left Haran. Abraham was an hundred years old when Isaac was born. 25 years.
Is any thing too hard for the LORD? At the time appointed I will return unto thee, according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son. (Genesis 18:14)
Hannah (1 Samuel 1)
And she was in bitterness of soul, and prayed unto the LORD, and wept sore. (1 Samuel 1:10)
For this child I prayed; and the LORD hath given me my petition which I asked of him. (1 Samuel 1:27)
Zacharias and Elisabeth (Luke 1)
KJV spells it Elisabeth.
And they had no child, because that Elisabeth was barren, and they both were now well stricken in years. (Luke 1:7)
Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John. (Luke 1:13)
Same words as Daniel: "Fear not... thy prayer is heard." A prayer prayed years earlier, still on record.
The man at the pool of Bethesda (John 5:1-9)

And a certain man was there, which had an infirmity thirty and eight years. When Jesus saw him lie, and knew that he had been now a long time in that case, he saith unto him, Wilt thou be made whole? (John 5:5-6)
Jesus saith unto him, Rise, take up thy bed, and walk. (John 5:8)
38 years waiting for the water to move. Jesus knew how long he'd been there.
Israel in Egypt (Exodus 2:23-24)
And God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob. (Exodus 2:24)
Honest "how long?" prayers
How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me? (Psalm 13:1)

I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry. He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings. (Psalm 40:1-2)
O LORD, how long shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear! (Habakkuk 1:2)
For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry. (Habakkuk 2:3)
When the answer is different from the ask
Paul's thorn (2 Corinthians 12:7-9)

And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure. For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me. And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. (2 Corinthians 12:7-9)
The thorn is called a messenger of Satan, which ties straight back to Job: Satan afflicts, God limits it and uses it.

Scripture never says what the thorn was. Some teachers suggest Paul's eyesight, based on Galatians 4:15 ("ye would have plucked out your own eyes, and have given them to me") and Galatians 6:11 ("how large a letter I have written unto you with mine own hand"). That's a possibility, not a stated fact. Paul's three days of blindness at conversion were healed when scales fell from his eyes (Acts 9:9, 18).
The cry is raised in chapter 6 and answered in chapter 19. Nothing prayed is lost.
The cry (fifth seal):

And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held: And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth? And white robes were given unto every one of them; and it was said unto them, that they should rest yet for a little season, until their fellowservants also and their brethren, that should be killed as they were, should be fulfilled. (Revelation 6:9-11)
The prayers rise:

And another angel came and stood at the altar, having a golden censer; and there was given unto him much incense, that he should offer it with the prayers of all saints upon the golden altar which was before the throne. And the smoke of the incense, which came with the prayers of the saints, ascended up before God out of the angel's hand. And the angel took the censer, and filled it with fire of the altar, and cast it into the earth: and there were voices, and thunderings, and lightnings, and an earthquake. (Revelation 8:3-5)
God answers:

Thou art righteous, O Lord, which art, and wast, and shalt be, because thou hast judged thus. For they have shed the blood of saints and prophets, and thou hast given them blood to drink; for they are worthy. (Revelation 16:5-6)

For true and righteous are his judgments: for he hath judged the great whore, which did corrupt the earth with her fornication, and hath avenged the blood of his servants at her hand. (Revelation 19:2)
Connect it:
Luke 18:7-8 promised God would avenge his own elect which cry day and night. Revelation shows that promise kept.
And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death. (Revelation 12:11)
We started with "why the delay?" We end with "you were heard, you are loved, be strong while you wait."

Then said he unto me, Fear not, Daniel: for from the first day that thou didst set thine heart to understand, and to chasten thyself before thy God, thy words were heard, and I am come for thy words. (Daniel 10:12)

And said, O man greatly beloved, fear not: peace be unto thee, be strong, yea, be strong. And when he had spoken unto me, I was strengthened, and said, Let my lord speak; for thou hast strengthened me. (Daniel 10:19)
Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world. (1 John 4:4)

sections.heading: Study Notes and Reflection

content.text: Clarifications to keep the study accurate:
Lucifer
(Isaiah 14) and the
King of Tyrus
(Ezekiel 28) are addressed to human kings. Many read Satan behind them, especially in Ezekiel 28:13-15 ("Thou hast been in Eden the garden of God")
Prince of Persia
is a ruler in Satan's kingdom, not one of his names
Daniel's prayer
wasn't blocked. It was heard day one. The answer was resisted
Paul's eyesight
as the thorn is a possibility, not stated in scripture
The man born blind
and the
man at Bethesda
show long affliction and God's timing. Neither is recorded praying for healing

reflection_questions: What have I been praying about that feels delayed? Have I stopped praying?
Where might I be fighting flesh and blood when the battle is spiritual?
Which piece of the armour am I neglecting?
Like Job, can I worship in the middle of loss, before the restoration?
Like Paul, can I receive "My grace is sufficient" if the answer is different from my ask?
What does it change to know my words were heard from the first day?

wordStudies.meaning: To afflict, humble, bow down low.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: Daniel's fast was humbling himself before God. It's the same word as "afflict your souls" on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:29). Fasting is humility, not a hunger strike to force God's hand.

wordStudies.meaning: To hear with attention, to hear and respond.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: God's hearing is never passive. He heard, and the answer was sent that same day.

wordStudies.meaning: To stand, take a stand. Here with "before me": stood against me, face to face.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: The prince stood in the way and blocked it. That's resistance, not refusal. The answer was already on its way.

wordStudies.meaning: Prince, captain, chief, ruler.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: The SAME word describes Michael in the same verse, "one of the chief princes." So the prince of Persia isn't the human king. He's a spiritual ruler on Michael's level, which is why the answer was held 21 days. See also Daniel 10:20 and Daniel 12:1.

wordStudies.meaning: "Who is like God?"
wordStudies.what_it_changes: His name is a question with one answer: nobody. The enemy said "I will be like the most High" (Isaiah 14:14). He's opposed by the angel whose very name says no one is.

wordStudies.meaning: Desired, precious, treasured.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: Before the explanation, before the battle report, God calls Daniel treasured. Said again in Daniel 10:19 and earlier in Daniel 9:23.

wordStudies.meaning: To be strong, make firm, take hold.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: Said twice, then Daniel says "I was strengthened," the same word. The command came with the power to obey it.

wordStudies.meaning: Adversary, one who opposes. The verb means to resist, to accuse.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: In Zechariah 3:1 he stands "to resist him," and that's the verb form of his own name. His name is his job description.

wordStudies.meaning: Slanderer, false accuser. From a verb meaning to throw across.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: He works by throwing accusations between you and God, and between you and other people.

wordStudies.meaning: A prosecutor who brings charges in court.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: It's a courtroom word, and yet we have a defense lawyer: "we have an advocate with the Father" (1 John 2:1), Greek parakletos G3875.

wordStudies.meaning: Shining one, morning star. The root means to shine, and also to boast.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: His name holds his glory and his fall at once: brightness that turned into boasting. Jesus is the real one: "the bright and morning star" (Revelation 22:16).

wordStudies.meaning: A rock.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: God is the Rock: "He is the Rock, his work is perfect" (Deuteronomy 32:4). Then: "their rock is not as our Rock" (Deuteronomy 32:31). Tyrus is the false rock set against the true one.

wordStudies.meaning: To cover, screen, overshadow, protect.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: It's the same word for the cherubim "covering the mercy seat with their wings" (Exodus 25:20). He was a guardian over God's presence, and he fell from there.

wordStudies.meaning: Worthlessness, without profit.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: His name means worthless. Everything he offers ends in nothing.

wordStudies.meaning: Lord of the fly. The false god of Ekron.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: King Ahaziah sent to Baalzebub instead of God, and Elijah asked, "Is it not because there is not a God in Israel?" (2 Kings 1:3).

wordStudies.meaning: To cause to wander, to lead astray.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: Our word "planet" (a wandering star) comes from the same root. Deception is a slow drift off course, not a sudden fall.

wordStudies.meaning: To change the outward appearance, to disguise.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: "Be ye transformed" in Romans 12:2 is a different word, metamorphoo G3339, a change from within. Satan changes his costume. God changes your nature.

wordStudies.meaning: Destruction (Hebrew) and destroyer (Greek).
wordStudies.what_it_changes: John gives the name in both languages so no one misses it: he destroys. Jesus came "that they might have life" (John 10:10).

wordStudies.meaning: To fence in, to hedge about, as with thorns.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: Satan admits the hedge is there. The enemy could see God's protection around Job before Job could.

wordStudies.meaning: Literally "to bless."
wordStudies.what_it_changes: In Job 1:11 and Job 2:9 the Hebrew literally says "bless God." It's a polite stand-in. The writer wouldn't put "curse God" on the page.

wordStudies.meaning: To demand, to ask to have someone handed over.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: Satan had to ask, just like with Job. And "you" is plural in Greek: he wanted all of them. "I have prayed for thee" is singular: Jesus prayed for Peter by name.

wordStudies.meaning: To shake grain in a sieve.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: Sifting separates. What's left after the shaking is what's real. Peter came out of it called to "strengthen thy brethren."

wordStudies.meaning: Schemes, a planned method.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: It's where our word "method" comes from. His attacks are strategic, not random. Look at Job: stacked and timed.

wordStudies.meaning: Wrestling, hand-to-hand combat.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: This is a close-range fight, not arrows from a distance. It's personal.

wordStudies.meaning: First in rank, authorities, world-rulers.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: These are ranks, a chain of command. That's exactly what Daniel 10 shows: a prince over Persia, another over Grecia.

wordStudies.meaning: The heavenly realms.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: It's the same word for where we're seated with Christ, "in heavenly places" (Ephesians 2:6). The battle is in that realm, and we're seated above it.

wordStudies.meaning: To lose heart, give up, grow weary.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: Jesus told the parable for one reason: so we don't quit while we wait.

wordStudies.meaning: Literally to hit under the eye, give a black eye.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: The judge was afraid she'd wear him out. If persistence gets through to an unjust judge, how much more to a loving Father.

wordStudies.meaning: Shamelessness.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: The friend got the bread because he wasn't embarrassed to keep knocking. Bold, shameless prayer.

wordStudies.meaning: To wait, look for, hope. Also to bind together like a twisted cord.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: The Hebrew doubles the verb: "waiting, I waited." It's the same word as "they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength" (Isaiah 40:31).

wordStudies.meaning: Two different words. "Though it tarry" means to linger. "It will not tarry" means to be late.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: It may linger from where you stand, and yet it will not be late on God's clock.

wordStudies.meaning: Messenger. The same word translated "angel."
wordStudies.what_it_changes: Paul's thorn was an angel of Satan sent to harass him, the same unseen conflict as Daniel 10.

wordStudies.meaning: To strike with the fist.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: It's the same word for what was done to Jesus: "and buffeted him" (Matthew 26:67). Paul suffered what his Lord suffered.

wordStudies.meaning: To finish, complete, bring to its goal.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: It's the word in "It is finished" (John 19:30). God's strength does its finished work in our weakness.

wordStudies.meaning: To pitch a tent over, to dwell upon.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: Christ's power doesn't just visit the weakness. It moves in and camps over it.

wordStudies.meaning: To vindicate, to do justice for someone.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: The martyrs aren't asking for revenge. They're asking God to prove them right. "Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord" (Romans 12:19).

wordStudies.meaning: Incense, a burnt offering of sweet spices.
wordStudies.what_it_changes: "Let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense" (Psalm 141:2). Prayers are gathered and offered. None of them are lost.
